verdict: Avoid new sponge iron and ferro alloy exposure in Raipur; the data call is Avoid and the local news is worse, so only existing good accounts with full security and monthly monitoring should be touched.
title: Raipur sponge iron & ferro alloys: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Raipur sponge iron or ferro alloy unit buys iron ore and coal, burns them with power in a kiln or furnace, and sells a commodity priced off steel and ore indices.** Cash comes in from long steel makers and traders, often on credit, while ore, coal and power are paid for up front. **The value sits in the spread between input cost and realisation, not in the asset** — a kiln earns only when it runs at load and power is cheap. So when a proposal lands, check the power tariff and the ore linkage first; if either is open-market, ask for the last twelve months of landed cost per tonne.

## Where cash and capex sit now
**Power is the swing cost and it has broken.** Chhattisgarh steel mills are reporting production disruption and rising costs from severe power shortages [1]. **Local demand is also lagging: Chhattisgarh GST collections grew 2.4% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and electricity demand grew 6.7% against India's 9.5% [D].** India-wide IIP for NIC 24 (basic metals) grew only 2.4% YoY [D], and Brent at $113/bbl sits above the $75–100 band [D], which lifts freight and coal-linked costs. **Capex is heavy and lumpy** — one Raipur district steel expansion is listed at Rs 8221 million [3], and a peer's project covers a 1,000-TPD sponge iron plant, a 21-MVA ferro alloy unit, a 33-MW WHRB plant and a 12-MW CFBC plant [11]. So when a proposal lands for a new kiln or furnace, check whether power is tied to a captive or WHRB source; if it is not, ask for the power purchase agreement and the tariff escalation clause.

## What the peers tell us
**Integrated players are holding up, standalone ones are not.** Shyam Metalics reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 52.4 billion and operating EBITDA of Rs 7.27 billion, with revenue up 27% YoY and volumes up 22% [4]; Q3 FY26 revenue was Rs 4,421 crore with a 12.2% operating EBITDA margin [7]. **But its sponge iron volume fell 2.33% YoY to 81,083 MT in March 2026 even as realisation rose 1.98% to Rs 25,656 per MT [5][6]** — price is carrying the number, not volume. **Older rating files show the small end is fragile:** one sponge unit ran working capital utilisation at ~91% with group exposure at 15.6% of net worth [10], and another saw operating margin drop to 4.1% in 11M FY2025 [11]. These rating reports are old (2018 and earlier) and should be read as pattern, not current fact.

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue integrated units with captive or waste-heat power, ferro alloy makers selling to stainless steel, and processors with ore linkage** — these are the borrowers whose cost base survives a power shock. **Avoid standalone sponge iron kilns buying open-market power and coal, and any unit whose group entities absorb cash** [10]. Structure term debt to match the kiln's ramp, keep the working capital limit tight against the assessed cycle, and take a monthly stock-and-receivables statement, a power bill copy and a production log every month. **Take a covenant on power cost per tonne and on promoter contribution before any expansion drawdown** [11].

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the power bill and the kiln load factor monthly; a rising bill with falling load is the first crack** [1]. **Watch GST and electricity demand for the state quarterly** — both are running below India [D], so a further gap means local offtake is weakening. **Watch sponge iron realisation against the Rs 25,656 per MT peer print [5]; a fall with flat volume means margin is being given away.** And watch any request to fund a new kiln or furnace without a captive power line [11] — that is the proposal to decline.
